articles.title: Caitlin Clark leaves fans speechless as she reveals how she wrapped up one of her busiest months
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark turned a month filled with games and big performances into a post.
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark turned a month filled with games and big performances into a post.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark had an August that was difficult to sum up in a single image . The Indiana Fever star went through a month packed with games, important moments and performances that helped keep her team in the fight near the top of the WNBA , but she has now decided to look back and preserve some of those days in a much more personal way.

The basketball star shared an August recap on Instagram featuring different images from what she has experienced over the past few weeks. Some of them were related to basketball, while others captured small details from the days surrounding each game, offering a different look at a month that ended up being especially intense for her .

August had a little bit of everything for Caitlin Clark

Indiana's schedule did not give Clark much room to slow down. During August, the Fever played 11 games, finishing with a 7-4 record during a crucial stretch of the regular season with the Playoffs approaching.

The month began with two consecutive losses against the Minnesota Lynx and Las Vegas Aces , but Indiana quickly responded. The Fever then picked up wins against the Chicago Sky, New York Liberty, Dallas Wings, Atlanta Dream and Toronto Tempo , before suffering another loss to Dallas and another against New York.

The final stretch looked different. Indiana dominated Chicago on August 23 and closed out the month with another convincing victory, this time a 111-91 win over the Connecticut Sun .

And it was in that final game that Clark put the finishing touch on a strong month on the court.

The final game turned into a special night

Against Connecticut, Clark delivered one of her best performances of the month. In 34 minutes, she finished with 34 points, 12 assists, 5 rebounds and 3 steals, while shooting 6-for-12 from three-point range .

The 12 assists carried extra significance, as they pushed her past the 300-assist mark for the season.

But Clark's recap was not limited to what happened during the 40 minutes of each game.

Then came the details Caitlin wanted to keep

Among the images she chose to remember August is an opening photo of Clark holding several pairs of basketball sneakers. The scene feels like a small glimpse into everything that has accompanied her demanding schedule throughout the month .

Other photos show different moments from her days around the games. In one, she wears black Nike sweatpants with white stripes, white sneakers, her hair down and headphones, while another shows her in brown Nike sweatpants , a white hoodie and white sneakers, again with her hair down.

They are simple details, but that is precisely what makes the recap interesting: it is not all about statistics or results. Clark also chose to preserve small scenes from before the games and the moments that make up the routine of such a demanding season.

Among all the images from August, her post ultimately became something of an album capturing what this summer has looked like for her.

A summer that can also be measured in numbers

Beyond the photographs, Clark's current form helps explain why August carried so much weight.

The Indiana guard is averaging 22.5 points and 8.4 assists per game during the 2026 season . After dealing with back discomfort midway through the campaign, she also reached the end of August saying that she was in the best physical condition of her career.

But now, the pace is about to change completely.

The WNBA will enter a break from August 31 through September 16 because of the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Germany .

Clark will join Team USA for the tournament before returning to Indiana for the final games of the regular season. The Fever will be back in action on September 18 against Toronto Tempo, followed by games against the Washington Mystics and Minnesota Lynx before the Playoffs begin .

articles.title: Team USA loses two stars just before the FIBA World Cup: A"ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum will not travel
articles.standfirst: The United States makes its debut this Friday against China with two hugely significant absences at the FIBA World Cup.
articles.summary: The United States makes its debut this Friday against China with two hugely significant absences at the FIBA World Cup.
articles.body:
'A A"ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum will not be able to compete in the tournament due to health issues and are forcing Team USA to alter its plans when the countdown is already underway.'

The United States announced this Monday the withdrawal of both players, who will be replaced by their Washington teammates Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron.

Two absences that change the outlook

The absence of both players shook the start of the women's basketball World Cup.

The absence of A"ja is especially significant. The Las Vegas Aces star, a four-time WNBA MVP , arrived as one of the team's leaders.

With her selection, Wilson was chosen as the standout player of the Paris 2024 Olympic Games and the 2022 World Cup . The United States loses a gem for the meeting of the best national teams in the world.

During the first part of the season, the player had borne a significant workload and needed time to rest

"In Plum's case, she has had a calf injury for a long time, and she has played a large part of the WNBA season with it without recovering 100%. It is also a hard blow for the national team.

The unexpected opportunity for Iriafen and Citron

The story now has two new protagonists. Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron, teammates in Washington , will be responsible for filling the spots left by Wilson and Plum .

Both had previously participated in the national team's camps, but now the situation is completely different: they will have the chance to be part of the team that will try to defend the historic dominance of the United States in the World Cups.

The original Team USA roster had already been announced in early August and was led by names such as Caitlin Clark, Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, Paige Bueckers, Angel Reese and Wilson herself. Plum was also part of that group of 12 players.

Now, just days before the debut, the United States will have to face the World Cup without two of its most experienced stars. The objective remains the same: to lift the trophy again. But the road to that fifth consecutive title has just become more complicated.

articles.title: Angel Reese avoids suspension after WNBA rescinds controversial eighth technical foul
articles.summary: Angel Reese avoided an automatic one-game suspension after the WNBA rescinded what had initially been ruled her eighth technical foul of the season. The call came after an incident with Portland’s Carla Leite, but the league reversed it shortly after the game. Reese remains at seven technical fouls and will not receive the $1,500 fine or suspension.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark looks back and ranks the defining moments of her WNBA and NCAA career
articles.standfirst: Clark has established many records during her career in Iowa and Indiana
articles.summary: Clark has established many records during her career in Iowa and Indiana
articles.body:
The 30th WNBA season is on a short break until September 17th due to the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, and when the action returns all 15 teams will play the final four remaining games in their schedule during the last week of the regular season, which concludes on September 24 .

These final games will serve to sort out playoff seedings and major individual honors. In the MVP race , the battle has narrowed down to a fierce two-player contest between four-time winner A'ja Wilson , who is a last-minute withdrawal from the World Cup due to health reasons and is leading the league in scoring for a third consecutive year.

The other player is Caitlin Clark , whose unprecedented offensive production accounts for a staggering 41.4 points created per game , standing as the highest mark in league history backed by 22.5 PPG and a league-leading 8.4 APG .

Caitlin Clark Ranks Her Top Career Milestones

With the league on pause, State Farm , one of Caitlin Clark's premier sponsors, produced a feature video asking the superstar guard to rank her defining basketball moments across her legendary NCAA run with Iowa and her professional career with the Indiana Fever , where she has already established numerous all-time records.

Clark noted that every milestone holds a unique place in her journey, but she awarded the top spot to the historic shot against Michigan in 2024 that officially crowned her the NCAA all-time leading scorer , men and women included.

Clark finished her collegiate career in Iowa City with an astonishing 3,951 total points , a standard that looks virtually unbreakable given her career average of nearly 30 points per game.

Taking second place on her personal list was capturing the Rookie of the Year award , punctuated by a historic debut campaign where she set single-season rookie records for points (769) , three-pointers ( 122 ), and assists ( 337 ).

Rounding out the podium at third was the milestone night she secured her first WNBA triple-double , registering 19 points, 12 rebounds, and 13 assists , to become the first rookie in league history and the first Fever player to accomplish the feat in a victory over New York.

From All-Star Highlights to Overcoming Early Rookie Struggles

The fourth entry on Clark's countdown highlighted her appearance in the WNBA All-Star Game against Team USA prior to the Paris Olympic Games.

That showcase stands as the most-watched All-Star Game in league history , and Clark added to the spectacle by setting the rookie single-game assist record with 10 dimes while leading her squad to victory.

Taking the fifth spot was reaching the 1,000 career point threshold during the opening game of this season, a milestone she humbly admitted carried little personal weight at the moment since she wasn't even tracking when it happened.

Finally, rounding out the list at sixth, Clark looked back at her very first professional regular-season game, a tough loss to the Connecticut Sun where she finished with 20 points alongside a WNBA debut-record 10 turnovers .

Now, at just 24 years old and playing the most dominant basketball of her life, Clark is positioned to add plenty of new unforgettable chapters to her resume over the final stretch of this season and for years to come.

articles.title: Enes Kanter calls for WNBA ‘peace summit’ as Caitlyn Jenner agrees to moderate debate
articles.standfirst: The former NBA player's latest challenge is part of a broader campaign he has launched in recent weeks
articles.summary: The former NBA player's latest challenge is part of a broader campaign he has launched in recent weeks
articles.body:
F ormer NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom is escalating his campaign against the WNBA’s transgender eligibility policies, this time with a proposal he says could bring one of sports’ most divisive debates into the open. Kanter has publicly challenged WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert to participate in what he calls a “peace summit,” a public discussion about the league’s eligibility rules.

According to Kanter, Olympic gold medalist and television personality Caitlyn Jenner has already agreed to serve as moderator if the event takes place. The proposal marks the latest chapter in a controversy that has placed the former NBA veteran at the center of a growing conversation about gender eligibility in women's sports.

Kanter takes direct aim at WNBA leadership

In a post on X, Kanter framed the proposed summit as an opportunity for a transparent and respectful discussion rather than another round of private meetings and public statements. “The whole world is laughing at you. You have turned the WNBA into a laughingstock,” Kanter wrote, directing his criticism toward league leadership.

He then called on Engelbert and the league to engage in a public conversation. “Let's have the peace summit. No shouting. No hiding. No carefully scripted statements,” Kanter added. According to Kanter, Jenner is willing to moderate the discussion, which he believes would allow all sides to address questions surrounding the league’s policies in front of a national audience.

“Let's sit across the table from each other, have an open and respectful conversation, and address the questions millions of people are asking,” he wrote. As of Monday, the WNBA had not publicly responded to Kanter's proposal.

A campaign that has drawn national attention

Kanter's latest challenge is part of a broader campaign he has launched in recent weeks. The former Boston Celtics, New York Knicks and Oklahoma City Thunder center first drew headlines when he declared himself eligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft . His argument centered on what he claims is a lack of specificity in the league's eligibility language regarding biological sex and transgender participation.

The WNBA's collective bargaining agreement states that players must be women, but Kanter has argued that the policy leaves unanswered questions regarding definitions and eligibility standards. His comments quickly generated reactions across the sports world, with supporters praising his willingness to raise the issue and critics dismissing the effort as a publicity stunt.

The debate intensified further when Kanter attended a game between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever wearing a shirt that read: “WOMAN: noun. adult human female.” The appearance ended with Kanter being escorted from Chicago's Wintrust Arena. He was later informed that he was banned from the venue, a development that only increased media attention surrounding his campaign.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark ranks behind one star as the best college player ever according to the future WNBA Rookie of the Year
articles.standfirst: Although she never became a national champion, Caitlin Clark holds several NCAA records
articles.summary: Although she never became a national champion, Caitlin Clark holds several NCAA records
articles.body:
With the WNBA season in a break due to the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, it's a good time to remember that the jump from college basketball to the pros is not easy for everyone, but recent rookies who will represent Team USA in the World Cup like Rhyne Howard , Aliyah Boston , Caitlin Clark , Angel Reese , and Paige Bueckers have exceeded expectations, putting the bar high for newcomers.

This season it's the second overall pick Olivia Miles who has excelled, acting as the engine for the best team in the league while firmly entering MVP conversations alongside A'ja Wilson and Caitlin Clark , with the Rookie of the Year award looking like a total lock for her.

Through 38 games, Miles is averaging 19.7 PPG and 6.0 APG , both leading her squad and ranking inside the top eight across the entire WNBA . She has accumulated a total of 749 points , sitting just 20 points behind Caitlin Clark's all-time rookie record of 769 points , and with four games left to play, it is only a matter of time before she establishes a brand-new rookie scoring standard.

Olivia Miles Places Caitlin Clark Just Behind Breanna Stewart in NCAA History

During her stellar collegiate career split between Notre Dame and TCU , Miles accomplished remarkable feats, including becoming the first freshman in tournament history, men's or women's, to log a triple-double , though she never quite reached the ultimate national championship game.

While she never squared off directly against Caitlin Clark's Iowa squad on the college hardwood, Miles readily acknowledges CC's extraordinary greatness, ultimately ranking her as the second-best player in NCAA history , positioned directly behind legendary icon Breanna Stewart.

In a featured media segment following her draft selection, Miles was prompted to navigate a bracket-style format weighing various historical women’s basketball luminaries, a process that steadily winnowed the field down to a final pairing of Clark and Stewart .

When forced to make the definitive selection, Miles leaned toward Stewart. "See, this is hard," Miles explained. "Caitlin has the scoring, the assists. Stewie has four chips and four MVPs. I’m just gonna have to go Stewie just based off her dominance and winning. "

Weighing Championship Rings Against Historic All-Time Scoring Records

Opting for Stewart is hard to argue against statistically, given that she finished her collegiate run with an astonishing 151-5 overall record , captured four consecutive national championships at UConn, earned the Final Four Most Outstanding Player award four times , and stands alone as the only player in women's college basketball history to secure that honor during every single tournament appearance of her career.

On the other hand, Clark carved out a completely different yet equally immortal legacy, leading the Iowa Hawkeyes to back-to-back National Championship appearances while wrapping up her historic tenure as the NCAA Division I all-time leading scorer across both men's and women's basketball with 3,951 career points .

As a two-time national player of the year , Clark also swept the all-time tournament records for total points, assists, and three-pointers , proving that whether one values Stewart's unmatched hardware or Clark's revolutionary statistical dominance, both guards represent the absolute pinnacle of the collegiate game.

articles.title: Could the connection between Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese become the surprise of the World Cup?
articles.standfirst: For years, they starred in one of the most talked-about rivalries in women's basketball, fueling expectations about what could happen when the two stars meet at the FIBA World Cup.
articles.summary: For years, they starred in one of the most talked-about rivalries in women's basketball, fueling expectations about what could happen when the two stars meet at the FIBA World Cup.
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark and Angel Reese have starred in one of the most followed rivalries in women's basketball in recent years. Today, with the possibility of seeing them together on Team USA, a question arises: What kind of connection can they show when they share the court?

A video released today quickly put both figures in the spotlight, sharing a moment during a game that was recorded earlier but that points to a great partnership for what is to come in Berlin.

“Her connection in Berlin will be different”

The message shared by the TNT Sport U.S signal was accompanied by a direct reference to Berlin and the possibility that the dynamic between Clark and Reese could reach a new dimension there.

“That CC and Angel Reese court chemistry” , the network wrote, before dropping a phrase that left the door open to all kinds of expectations.

articles.title: Angel Reese matches Caitlin Clark with a WNBA first no other player has accomplished this season
articles.standfirst: For the second week in a row and for the fourth time in her career, Reese was named Player of the Week
articles.summary: For the second week in a row and for the fourth time in her career, Reese was named Player of the Week
articles.body:
Since entering the league in 2024 both Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark have rewritten the history books, with Clark setting a new season high in assists ( 337 ) during her rookie campaign, a record that was broken the following year with 357 , alongside recording the most assists in a single game with 19 .

Meanwhile, Reese is thoroughly enjoying her new chapter after being traded to Atlanta this season, where she has shattered the WNBA single-season record for most double-doubles with 29 .

She has also rewritten single-game and single-season rebounding standards that feature hauling down 26 boards in a single contest and accumulating 485 total rebounds , a milestone benchmark she aims to push even higher before the regular season concludes as she chases becoming the first player ever to reach 500 rebounds in a single year .

Angel Reese Matches Caitlin Clark With Elite Weekly Honor

Both of those historic rebounding milestones for Reese occurred last week, prompting the WNBA to award her the Eastern Conference Player of the Week honor for the second consecutive week and the fourth time in her professional career, following a dominant stretch where she averaged 14.0 PPG, 17.7 RPG, and 3.7 APG .

With this latest accolade, Reese joins Caitlin Clark as the only players in the league to capture back-to-back Player of the Week awards this season.

Now, as both stars prepare to join forces as teammates for the United States at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, they will soon return to WNBA action where Atlanta and Indiana are projected to face off in a high-voltage playoff series, as both squads look to cement the fourth and fifth seeds in the standings to set up what would undoubtedly be the most-watched postseason series in league history.

articles.title: Angel Reese closes out a historic summer and an unexpected post steals the spotlight
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta Dream star closed out August with a post featuring some of the moments that defined her past few weeks.
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream star closed out August with a post featuring some of the moments that defined her past few weeks.
articles.body:
Without a doubt, August was a busy month for Angel Reese. The player appeared in 10 games with the Atlanta Dream, eight of which ended in victories , a run that ultimately secured the team a spot in the Playoffs.

Individually, she averaged 17 points, 14.5 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game . Her consistency also earned her consecutive Eastern Conference Player of the Week honors .

And while those numbers would already be enough to stand out, Angel took things to another level.

Three records that changed her August

On August 22, Angel recorded 31 points and 14 rebounds against the Phoenix Mercury , setting a new season-high in scoring. Just two days later came the performance that made history.

Against the Los Angeles Sparks, she grabbed 26 rebounds, the most ever recorded by a player in a single game in WNBA history . That same night, she also broke the record for most rebounds in a single season.

Her final major milestone came on August 30, when she posted 15 points and 11 rebounds against the Minnesota Lynx to record her 29th double-double of the year .

But if anything has become clear, it is that Angel has also turned her social media into a space where she shares some of her biggest moments, and this summer closeout was no exception. The player posted a recap featuring several photos from on and off the court, including one with a young fan posing beside her while Angel holds her own Barbie . Beyond the moment itself, the photo reflects the connection the star has built with her youngest admirers.

A different side of her style

Fashion also had a place in the recap. In one of the photos, Angel wears a red jacket, black pants, a red bag with thick white lines, dark sunglasses and matching shoes . Later, she completely changes the look with light-wash jeans, a black top, a belt, gold jewelry and a black bag.

A photo with Nneka Ogwumike

The collection also includes Nneka Ogwumike, one of the WNBA's most recognized figures. A champion, MVP, 11-time All-Star and president of the WNBPA , Ogwumike shares a moment with Angel as the two pose in a semi-embrace, showing the closeness they have developed within the league.

Their relationship is shaped by admiration and respect, and the photo offers a glimpse of the connections Angel has formed while building her own path in the WNBA.

September already has her next destination

Now, as a new month begins, the calendar enters a different stage. The WNBA will take a break for the international FIBA tournament , meaning Angel will not return to action with Atlanta until September 17.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese have to build a strong duo to adjust to the changes on Team USA
articles.standfirst: Two major absences put more responsibility on the younger core
articles.summary: Two major absences put more responsibility on the younger core
articles.body:
T he U.S. basketball team heading to the World Cup has made two considerable changes to its roster. Now, the younger players will have to build a solid team capable of competing for gold. Team USA enters the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup as the favorite, but the players will have to work together to achieve that goal.

Kelsey Plum and A’ja Wilson have been dropped from the roster for health reasons , paving the way for Mystics guard Sonia Citron and forward Kiki Iriafen. The changes come just days before Team USA tips off the tournament in Berlin, where the players are already preparing for their games.

Team chemistry will be key with two veterans out

Wilson has been dealing with a recurrent back issue over the last week and apparently did not want to exacerbate it. P lum, meanwhile, has been dealing with a calf issue for most of the season and did everything she could to make the World Cup squad, but could not meet the tight timeline.

The current Team USA roster now relies heavily on its young core to get the job done after two more veterans pulled out . The relationships within the roster will have to stand out, and there is plenty of excitement around seeing what the combination o f Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese will look like while playing on the same team.

Clark and Reese now have a chance to turn their rivalry into chemistry

The egos have to stay aside, with the rivalries left for the WNBA . More importantly, the players have to be honest about each other’s strengths so they can stand out as a team . Clark and Reese are known to have had some tension between them, and Caitlin has also recently had issues with Paige Bueckers, but those situations have to stay in the past. The goal now is to maximize what makes each of them some of the best players in the league.

Team USA enters as the heavy favorite to win the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup, with a roster full of generational talent. Even without four-time MVP A’ja Wilson, the U.S. has the best odds of winning the tournament.

Aliyah Boston, Paige Bueckers, Sonia Citron, Caitlin Clark, Napheesa Collier, Kahleah Copper, Chelsea Gray, Rhyne Howard, Kiki Iriafen, Angel Reese, Breanna Stewart and Jackie Young make up the 12-player roster. It is a strong group despite the late changes.

The U.S. roster is highlighted by athletes with extensive USA Basketball experience, combining for 10 Olympic and five World Cup gold medals. The team also features nine players making their World Cup debuts. Team USA is seeking its fifth consecutive World Cup gold medal and its 12th overall.
